title: Tools ready
hookLine: as doctors keep instruments ready, keep your principles ready (Meditations 3.13)

cards: Open the back of an ambulance. Nothing is in a drawer somewhere, waiting to be found. Every tool hangs exactly where a hand will reach for it, because when the call comes there's no time to search.
Marcus Aurelius knew doctors at close range: the physician Galen served at his court. In the thirteenth entry of book three he borrowed their habit for the inside of a person. Today: tools ready.

teach.b: Just as doctors always keep their instruments and knives at hand for sudden cases, Marcus writes, keep your principles ready, so you can understand things both divine and human. The point is speed.
A crisis rarely waits while you look up what you believe.

teach.h: DOGMATA: THE BELIEFS YOU LIVE BY.
teach.b: The Greek word is dogmata, the beliefs you actually live by. Not a library of quotations, but a short kit you can reach without thinking. This week gave a few: as it is, judge carefully, only this.
Each is small enough to hang on a hook inside you.

Then Marcus adds: do everything, even the smallest thing, remembering how the divine and the human are bound together. You won't do anything human well without that larger view, he says, and the reverse.
For a Stoic, the kit isn't only for emergencies. It's for washing the dishes and answering the email too. And practice makes ready.
A surgeon's hand finds the scalpel because it has found it a thousand times. Principles work the same way. Read once, they're decoration.
Used daily, they become reflex. That's why Marcus wrote the same few ideas again and again in his notebook. He wasn't forgetful.
He was drilling. So the real question isn't, do I have good principles? Most people do.
It's, could I reach one in three seconds, when the phone rings with bad news, or someone snaps at me in a parking lot?

how: Many readers of Marcus Aurelius keep a few short principles written on a card or in a notebook, rereading them so they can be reached quickly in a hard moment.

games.q: someone cuts in front of you at the pharmacy, and you feel the heat rise. you have three seconds. what fits 3.13?
o: reach for one principle you keep ready.
decide to read some philosophy tonight.
games.why: Marcus wants principles hung where the hand finds them, like a doctor's instruments: ready before the sudden case.

practice: Choose three principles you want within reach this week, each short enough to say in one breath: lines from this path, like as it is or keep faith, or words of your own. If you have a card or your phone's notes, write them down.
Read them once, slowly, and picture reaching for one in a hard moment.

wordCard.voice: Tools ready. Marcus says keep your principles at hand the way doctors keep their instruments, ready for the sudden case. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek, 'things that seem right': principles, the beliefs a Stoic keeps ready. Singular dogma.

carryVoice: Your line: keep your principles ready. Like a doctor's kit, close at hand. See you tomorrow.
